clue.text: Getting 20 out of 24, this year's top dogs?

definitions.text: Getting 20 out of 24, this year's top dogs?

parts.words: Getting 20 out of 24, this year's top dogs?
parts.note: the team that took the clean sweep in the annual rugby tournament of Europe's half-dozen countries are this season's top dogs, and a breed from that island fits the canine reading

explanation.surface: A question about which side, having swept the tournament, are this season's leading dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is THE GRAND SLAM and 24 is SIX NATIONS, the European rugby championship; Ireland won the Grand Slam that year, so their players are the top dogs, and the breed of dog completes the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of wiry red-coated dog from Ireland, here punning on the Irish rugby team as champions.

clue.text: Very exciting on left wing, tho' replaced

parts.note: the political left wing is called the Reds

indicators.note: replaced says the letters of the abbreviated word are put back in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, its three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that politics on the left became thrilling once something was swapped out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intensely thrilling or sensational is described idiomatically as scorching.

clue.text: Made an observation, a pithy one

definitions.meaning: past tense of see: noticed or witnessed something
a pithy observation is a proverb or saying

explanation.definitionFit: Saw is the past of see, and a saw is also an old proverb or maxim.

clue.text: Intent on achieving goal, held back by facile tackle

indicators.note: held back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone determined to reach an objective is restrained by an easy-looking tackle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held back by' carries both the reversal and the sense that the letters sit in 'facile tackle': CILET read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Telic is a philosophical term for directed towards an end or purpose.

clue.text: Making most of injury, raised a cheer

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters are read upwards, so backwards
most of says the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: harm is damage or injury

explanation.surface: A player exaggerating an injury gets the crowd shouting in support.
explanation.walkthrough: HARM loses its last letter to give HAR, which 'raised' turns upward into the cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rah is a shout of encouragement, as in rah-rah cheering.

clue.text: Terrible fellow one added to front row?

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
the van is the foremost rank or front line of an army

explanation.surface: A question about a fearsome forward joining the front row of the scrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'added to' is a link: I simply sits before VAN. The rugby 'front row' misleads; the van is the leading part of a force.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian tsar known by the epithet the Terrible bore this first name.

clue.text: Subject to teasing and reprimand, some beef

parts.note: to rib is to tease or mock gently
to roast is to criticise severely

explanation.surface: Being mocked and then told off feels like a slab of meat being prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: A rib roast is a cut of beef taken from the ribs and cooked whole.

clue.text: Showing class one way to revise this — sly

indicators.note: to revise something is to rework it, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cunning way of making something look classier is to rework it slyly.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant and fashionable, displaying good taste or classiness.

clue.text: Just some bloke-or the player of the championship

definitions.meaning: British slang for a person, an ordinary fellow
the initials of Brian O'Driscoll, the Irish centre named player of the Six Nations that year

explanation.definitionFit: Bod is slang for a chap, and also the nickname from the initials of rugby star Brian O'Driscoll.

clue.text: What every player strives to do in defeat

definitions.text: What every player strives to do
definitions.meaning: every competitor tries to do their utmost
to ... an opponent is to beat them

explanation.definitionFit: Doing one's utmost is doing one's best, and to best someone is to beat them.

clue.text: Cheesy toast from weak player in previous best team

parts.note: Wales won the Grand Slam the year before, so the previous champions were the Welsh
a rabbit is a poor or inept player in sport

explanation.surface: A dish of cheese on toast served up by a feeble player from last year's winning side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' and 'in' are links: the rabbit is one of the Welsh, and the pieces join in answer order.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is melted cheese on toast, also known by this older name.

clue.text: Bonnets men picked, in blue

definitions.meaning: flat woollen caps worn in Scotland
players capped for Scotland, whose rugby team plays in blue

explanation.definitionFit: These are Scottish bonnets, and punningly the caps awarded to players picked for Scotland.

clue.text: Back recent changes

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the preceding word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, its six letters rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like a verb meaning support, but it is a rugby noun: a centre is one of the backs.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby the centres are among the backs, the players behind the scrum.

clue.text: Bar supporters from these stations

definitions.meaning: the uprights that hold up the crossbar of a goal
places where people are positioned on duty

explanation.definitionFit: Goalposts hold up the crossbar, and a post is a station where someone is placed.

clue.text: Try, followed by a successful conclusion

definitions.text: Try, followed by a successful conclusion

parts.note: to have a go is to try

indicators.note: conclusion says take the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A rugby try is converted with a kick between the posts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'followed by' is a link putting the pieces in order. In rugby a try is followed by a conversion kick, which scores a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal is scored when a try is converted, and goal also means a successful aim.

clue.text: Attractive young women put on white jerseys

definitions.meaning: fresh-faced pretty girls with fair complexions
the red rose emblem is worn on England's white rugby shirts

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes fair-skinned pretty young women, and the red rose is England's emblem on its white kit.

clue.text: After a breather, one appears in cool garment

indicators.note: after puts the letter for one behind the breathing organ

parts.note: a lung is the organ one breathes with
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Once someone has caught their breath, they turn up dressed in something light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears in' is a link. A lungi is a cloth wrapped round the waist, worn in South Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A lungi is a loose cloth wrap worn in hot climates, so a garment that keeps one cool.

clue.text: Finish in style after S M second break in tour

indicators.note: after puts the phrase meaning finish behind the abbreviation for second

parts.note: to top off is to complete something with a flourish

explanation.surface: A tour party finishing elegantly after a pause.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'S M' printed in the held clue is stray OCR text, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopover, a short halt on a journey.

clue.text: Mislaid the cases, part A R R S G R 21 of Jack's luggage

indicators.note: mislaid suggests things put in the wrong place, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Losing the bags means part of a sailor's kit has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is a jack tar, a sailor. The words 'part A R R S G R 21 of' in the held clue are stray OCR text and links, not wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor traditionally kept belongings in a wooden box, which counts as baggage.

clue.text: In this display of overall supremacy, not missing a trick?

definitions.text: In this display of overall supremacy, not missing a trick?

parts.words: In this display of overall supremacy, not missing a trick?
parts.note: in bridge, winning every trick is the top contract; in rugby, beating every other nation is the same clean sweep

explanation.definitionFit: Winning all thirteen tricks in bridge, and in rugby beating every rival in the championship.

clue.text: N Measure that is needed R G A IN S E for ball game

parts.note: a foot is a unit of length
i.e. is the abbreviation of the Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A length unit and an explanatory phrase are what a sport requires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is needed for' is a link. The 'N' and 'R G A IN S E' in the held clue are stray OCR text.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British word for football, the game played with a ball.

clue.text: Spot extremes of eagerness — penalty

indicators.note: extremes of says take the first and last letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone notices a keenly contested penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, to notice.

clue.text: Some of the Lions, say, prepare for tour

definitions.meaning: the forwards of a rugby team such as the British and Irish Lions
to fill a suitcase before travelling

explanation.definitionFit: The forwards are a rugby side's pack, and to pack is to fill a case for a trip.

clue.text: Annual sporting event with a number of races

definitions.meaning: the yearly European rugby championship
a half-dozen peoples or countries

explanation.definitionFit: The yearly rugby championship of England, France, Ireland, Italy, Scotland and Wales, literally a half-dozen peoples.

clue.text: Approaches within earshot, taking part

indicators.note: taking part says only a portion of the words before it is used

explanation.surface: Someone joins in while staying close enough to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Comes closer to, draws towards.

clue.text: Part of pharmacy lecture relating to a certain class in chemistry

definitions.text: relating to a certain class in chemistry

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lecture to pharmacy students on a category of chemical compounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Acyl describes a group of organic radicals derived from carboxylic acids.

clue.text: Something to enjoy at breakfast -headline after English triumph?

definitions.meaning: bread soaked in egg and fried
a tabloid gloating that England have beaten France, burnt them

explanation.definitionFit: Eggy fried bread eaten in the morning, and punningly a headline saying the French are done for.

clue.text: At its best, leaves much to be desired?

definitions.text: At its best, leaves much to be desired?

parts.words: At its best, leaves much to be desired?
parts.note: a brew made from leaves is most wanted when it is at its best

explanation.definitionFit: A drink made by steeping leaves, much desired when well made.

clue.text: Score halved or score raised

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to net is to score a goal

explanation.surface: A tally cut in two or pushed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link. A score is twenty, so half of it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, and half of twenty is this number.

clue.text: Essay to which a couple of points might be added

definitions.meaning: an essay is an attempt

definitions.text: to which a couple of points might be added
definitions.meaning: a rugby touchdown can be followed by a conversion worth two points

explanation.definitionFit: An essay is an attempt, and in rugby a converted touchdown earns two extra points.

clue.text: Review internationals with no end of fervour and poetic lines

indicators.note: to review is to look over again, so the letters are reorganised

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A critic assesses international players and loses some passion while writing verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' means the R from 'end of fervour' is taken out of INTERNATIONALS before the rest are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A Petrarchan sonnet is fourteen lines of verse with an octave and sestet.
